name: Java4Shell
tldr: A bug in Java's Base64 decoder can let an attacker with no login run code. Exploit shown, not public; no attacks. Patch if all three hold: Java 17.0.6+ or Oracle's Java 8 Performance Pack, unpatched; a CPU with AVX-512 VBMI; untrusted Base64 input.
summary: A CPU check and a Java version check quickly narrow down whether you're exposed, since only newer Intel and AMD CPUs have AVX-512 VBMI; check every Java your apps actually use, including bundled ones. Proof-of-concept code for the memory corruption is public, but the researchers keep their working exploit chains private.

affected.label: Java 17.0.6+, 21, 25 or 27
affected.text: Any distribution (Oracle, Temurin, Corretto, Zulu, Red Hat…) without the November 2026 fix, plus Oracle's Java 8 Performance Pack (`8u511b33-perf`) and Oracle GraalVM for JDK 17/21. Standard Java 8 and 11 aren't affected.

affected.label: CPU has AVX-512 VBMI
affected.text: Intel Ice Lake or newer, AMD Zen 4 or newer (including Ryzen). ARM servers (Graviton, Ampere) never are. Run it where the app runs, on every node pool, because clusters often mix CPU generations.

affected.label: Untrusted input gets Base64-decoded
affected.text: Auth headers, tokens, SAML and uploads all qualify. Assume yes for anything internet-facing; researchers showed it against Jira, Confluence, Artifactory and Jenkins.

do.label: Patch Java
do.text: Oracle: 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1 (17 Nov). Corretto shipped all four lines on 17 Nov. Temurin's fixed builds are out for x64 Linux, Alpine and Apple-silicon Macs, but on 20 Nov not yet for Windows or the `eclipse-temurin` Docker images. Red Hat, Ubuntu and Debian have fixed packages. For Oracle's Java 8 Performance Pack, see Oracle's advisory.

do.label: Can't patch yet? Set this flag
do.text: Turns off only the vulnerable fast path. Needs a restart. Not an official Oracle workaround.

do.label: Check bundled Java
do.text: Common tools like Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and many others ship with their own Java. Updating the system Java doesn't fix them: update the tool, or set the flag in its own JVM settings. Red Hat still lists its Keycloak build, JBoss EAP OpenJDK 17 images and OpenShift Pipelines as affected. Appliances too: Cisco (for example Catalyst Center and Finesse) and Palo Alto (Privilege Threat Analytics, Remote Access Connector, the on-prem HTML5 Gateway) list affected products, and Fortinet is still checking. Their firewalls (Cisco ASA/FTD, PAN-OS, FortiOS) aren't affected.

changes.text: Clarified that the CPU and version checks help narrow it down but don't settle it: check every Java your apps use.
Cisco, Palo Alto and Fortinet appliance advisories added; PoC code for the memory corruption is public; Temurin Windows and Docker images still pending.
Corretto, Ubuntu and Debian fixes out; Temurin Windows and Docker images still pending. Oracle fixed builds now cited to Oracle. Safe versions added.
Review: Oracle's own fixed builds, Red Hat and Temurin fixes, GraalVM; 'disputed' note removed.
Added the CISA alert and Oracle's Java 8 Performance Pack exception.
